rv.q: The sections in which she interacts with her imaginary students are excellent, and she embodies the vibe of a frustrated teacher brilliantly. At no point do you get the impression that Miss June cares for her students; her job is simply a filler until she hits the big time.

Having secured a filming contract, she calls the production company to find out when they’re sending a car to pick her up. As it transpires, she didn’t secure a filming contract but somehow believed she did (despite never actually having signed one) and burned some bridges in telling other people so.
